content: He who is unable to live in society, or who has no need because he is sufficient for himself, must be either a beast or a god.
author: Aristotle
story:
This insight touches directly on the messy reality of human nature. From childhood, we are trained to fit in, to smooth over our eccentricities, and to mirror the expectations of those around us. But copying others only buys superficial acceptance at the cost of your own soul.

In Aristotle's view, genuine strength is not an abstract theory—it is a lived, daily practice. Your unique perspective and lived contradictions are your greatest offering to the world. The moment you stop performing and stand firmly in your own skin, you command an authority that imitation can never manufacture.
reflectionPrompt: In what area of your life are you overthinking the ideal approach instead of taking the simple, honorable action?
